outcome: Professor review now has an independent five-way scientific disposition model
owner_impact: Capability requests can now store Professor judgment independently from technical implementation lifecycle: Accept, Reject, Revise, Defer, or Future, with Pending reserved for unreviewed requests. Existing request IDs, evidence, candidate identities, provenance, approved/declined compatibility, in-progress work, and implemented capabilities remain intact. Professor guidance is stored separately from internal notes, and reviewed Revise/Defer/Future candidates remain unavailable but discoverable so they are not recreated as duplicates. This ticket does not yet replace the two-button inbox or expose the new semantics through the research-AI MCP.

next.text: Next is the Professor review interaction and MCP round-trip: replace the binary inbox controls with Accept, Reject, Revise, Defer and Future; expose sanitized decisions/guidance to research AI; and let Revise update the same candidate identity and return it to Pending. That work has not started yet.

technical_evidence: Professor disposition is stored separately from capability_requests.status and is constrained to pending, accepted, rejected, revise, deferred or future.
Legacy approved/in-progress/implemented rows backfill as accepted; declined rows as rejected; requested rows as pending.
A durable review-history table records each non-pending Professor decision without changing request or candidate identity.
Candidate capability and contract-delta surfaces synchronize only intentionally shareable Professor disposition/guidance while remaining candidate_unavailable until implementation.
Professor-only RLS and a restrictive insert policy prevent researchers from self-approving or creating pre-reviewed requests.
The existing triage RPC keeps approved/declined aliases compatible while accepting all five new decisions.
